title_candidates: ChatGPT health answers got better: use them differently
summary: OpenAI says GPT-5.5 Instant improves health answers for free ChatGPT users. The practical move is to use ChatGPT to prepare better questions, not replace care.

primary_source.title: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI says GPT-5.5 Instant brings stronger health responses to free ChatGPT users.
OpenAI says more than 230 million people use ChatGPT each week for health and wellness questions.
The company says GPT-5.5 Instant improved on health evaluations that look at accuracy, safety, communication, context awareness, completeness, and escalation.
OpenAI says a network of more than 260 physicians across 60 countries helped define and review health-response quality.

prerequisites: A non-emergency health question or appointment to prepare for

steps.instruction: Do not use ChatGPT for emergencies; call local emergency services or a clinician if symptoms are urgent.
Open ChatGPT and describe your question with age range, relevant symptoms, timing, medications, and what you already know.
Ask ChatGPT to list red flags that would require urgent care, then check whether any apply to you now.
Ask for three questions to bring to a doctor, pharmacist, insurer, or clinic.
Save the output as appointment notes, not as a diagnosis, and confirm decisions with a qualified professional.

risk_flags: Health article must avoid implying medical diagnosis or replacing professional care.
